explanations: /healthz is bound to the readiness handler, which pings Postgres and Redis and returns 503 when either is down or when draining. /healthz is the conventional liveness probe, so if the orchestrator uses it, a database or cache outage (or a shutdown drain) makes every pod fail liveness and get restarted. That does not fix the dependency, adds a restart storm and drops in-flight requests. Liveness should be shallow, like h.live. Separate /livez and /readyz are already provided, and each dependency check has its own timeout, so the readiness handler itself is sound.

Checks run in goroutines in parallel, and each has its own 800 ms context timeout, so the slow ping is cancelled around 800 ms and recorded as failed. Any failed check flips the status to 503. Neither sequential timing nor the 10 second hang applies.

On ctx.Done it calls health.Drain(), which makes ready answer 503 with status draining, sleeps 5 seconds, then calls http.Server.Shutdown with a bounded context so in-flight requests finish. It does not close the listener first and liveness is not involved.

The slice is preallocated and each goroutine receives its own index, so there are no overlapping writes; wg.Done and wg.Wait guarantee the writes are visible before the caller reads. Slices are not synchronized and the goroutines do run concurrently.
